hypotheses.justification: Mathlib's `class NumberField (K) [Field K] : Prop` has the fields `[to_charZero : CharZero K]` and `[to_finiteDimensional : FiniteDimensional ℚ K]` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Basic.lean). So the binder `[NumberField L₀]` already gives finite dimensionality over ℚ, through the instance `NumberField.to_finiteDimensional`. No other binder and not the conclusion needs this instance to elaborate. `TaylorWiles.ResidualRep (↥L₀) k` is an abbrev for `(L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L) →* Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) 𝕜` and only takes the section instances `[NumberField L]` and `[IsGalois ℚ L]`. `AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom` needs only `Normal ℚ L₀`, which the proof gets from `IsGalois.to_normal`. The proof never uses finite dimensionality. The helpers `liftAuxU` and `liftAuxU_spec` take only `[Normal ℚ ↥L₀]`. The surjectivity step `AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom_surjective` uses the normality instances and `Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)`, which the proof builds itself. The rest is `liftOfSurjective` and `liftOfRightInverse_comp_apply`. So the same proof should still go through once the binder is deleted, and if any step did need finiteness, `NumberField L₀` would supply it.
